title: Switch embedder to embeddinggemma-300m (768-dim)
description:
Replace Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit (~2.5GB, 2560-dim) with
google/embeddinggemma-300m (MLX, ~300MB, 768-dim) as the project embedder.

Why (app-wide, not just the Atlas):
  * A 300MB model can stay resident and embed a query string in milliseconds
    with no memory / GPU pressure -> the chunk HybridIndex can embed LIVE
    queries on every keystroke instead of degrading to BM25-only, and the
    Atlas focused-bullet affinity (see the search+affinity task) becomes
    reliable.
  * Leaves headroom for the ~2.5GB shared instruct LLM to coexist on 8GB.

Work:
  * python/embed_server.py + python/embed.py: load embeddinggemma via MLX,
    use its documented pooling (mean-pool, NOT Qwen's last-token), keep the
    same /embed HTTP contract.
  * Re-embed the corpus: clear every chunks.embedding_vec, let
    indexer.Backfiller repopulate; delete shuttle.hnsw so it rebuilds at the
    new dimension via LoadAndReconcile.
  * .fembed: bump format to version 2. The header already carries dims, so
    internal/ingest/embedfile only needs to accept dims=768 and version 2.
    Existing .fembed files are stale and must be regenerated offline.
  * VectorIndex / HNSW infers dimension from the vectors -> no Go signature
    change, but a mixed-dimension index is corrupt: block/flag search with an
    "index rebuilding" state until the re-embed completes.

Acceptance: live query embedding works in the evidence pane; go test ./...
green; a fresh boot rebuilds the HNSW at 768-dim without manual steps.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Sub-chunk evidence: surface the relevant span within a chunk
description:
Plan of record: sub_chunk_evaluation.md.

Today EvidenceFinder.Find (internal/web/evidence.go) shows trimRunes(c.Content, 320) — the first ~320 runes of each retrieved chunk, anchored at offset 0. Chunks are ~160-word transcript greedy chunks, so the pane shows roughly the first third regardless of where the match is. Downstream (transcript reader, ReaderSegment.CharStart, the excerpt form with hidden char_start/char_end/text) is already offset-aware; the missing pieces are (a) LOCATING the relevant span inside a chunk and (b) THREADING those offsets through the UI.

This epic covers the 15 steps in sub_chunk_evaluation.md. Phasing: steps 1-2 are the shippable MVP (lexical locator + match-centered <mark> snippet). Steps 3-7 thread offsets through the reader and excerpt form and tighten the query. Steps 8-15 are deeper retrieval work (passage re-scoring, provenance, semantic locator, dual-granularity indexing).

Prioritized above flying-shuttle-hkc and flying-shuttle-hs8.
close_reason: All 15 child tasks complete. Sub-chunk evidence localization shipped end to end: IDF/sentence/semantic/passage locators, match-centered <mark> snippets with stability + multi-span + per-sentence shading + expand-in-place, match provenance cues, span threaded into the transcript reader and excerpt form, keyboard cycling, and a dual-granularity passage index. ~20 commits on main.

title: Verify and tune hybrid BM25+Qwen3 search after ingest
description:
Now that Qwen3 embeddings can be imported via the ingest API, verify that the full hybrid search pipeline works end-to-end and tune it for good results.

Scope:
1. Confirm chunks imported from .fembed files are indexed in BOTH BM25 (HybridIndex.BM25) and HNSW (HybridIndex.Vector) — already wired in IndexChunks(), but needs smoke-test with real data.

2. Add search mode param to GET /api/v1/search:
   ?mode=hybrid (default) — RRF fusion of BM25 + HNSW vector results
   ?mode=bm25   — BM25 only (current query-time behaviour since embedder=nil)
   ?mode=vector — HNSW only (requires pre-computed query vector; skip for now or 501)
   This makes the mode explicit and testable without changing default behaviour.

3. Tune RRF k constant: current default k=60 was chosen for general use. With Qwen3 2560-dim vectors and the specific transcript-chunk domain, k may need adjustment. Add SHUTTLE_RRF_K env var (default 60) so it can be tuned at runtime without recompile.

4. Add ?limit param to search endpoint (currently hardcoded to 10 in handler). Surface it as a query param with a sensible max cap (e.g. 100).

Acceptance: after importing a .fembed file, a BM25 query for a keyword known to be in a chunk returns that chunk, AND (once vector index is populated) an HNSW-adjacent chunk also surfaces via the hybrid mode.
close_reason: Implemented ?mode=hybrid|bm25|vector, SHUTTLE_RRF_K env var, limit capped at 100. Shipped in 8f9aafb.

title: Ingest existing .embed files into system
description:
One-time operational task: convert and load all existing .embed TSV files into the SQLite store and HNSW index.

Prerequisites: flying-shuttle-7p6 (Python converter) OR flying-shuttle-vv9 (Go native import) must be complete.

Recommended path once vv9 is done (no Python needed):
  curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy     -H 'Content-Type: application/json'     -d '{"path": "/absolute/path/to/file.embed"}'

Or batch via directory (requires .fembed conversion first):
  python embed.py --convert --embed-dir ./embeddings/
  curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest/directory     -d '{"path": "/absolute/path/to/embeddings"}'

Verification:
- Check SQLite: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(embedding_vec) FROM chunks;
  → COUNT(*) should equal number of records in .embed file(s)
  → COUNT(embedding_vec) should equal COUNT(*) (all chunks have vectors)
- Check HNSW: server log should show 'loaded HNSW index from shuttle.hnsw (N vectors)' on restart
- Test search: POST /api/v1/search?q=<term> should return results
close_reason: No longer desired: existing .embed files will not be imported; fresh embeddings will be generated instead.

title: Add native Go .embed TSV importer (no Python required)
description:
Add a Go reader for the legacy .embed TSV format so existing files can be ingested directly via the API without a Python conversion step.

New file: internal/ingest/embedfile/tsv_reader.go

type TSVReader struct { ... }
func OpenTSV(path string) (*TSVReader, error)  // opens and validates header
func (r *TSVReader) Next() (*Record, error)    // reuses same Record type as .fembed reader
func (r *TSVReader) Close() error

Implementation:
- Use encoding/csv with tab delimiter and csv.LazyQuotes=true
- Read and validate header row: [file_name, start_token, embedding, text]
- Per row: parse start_token as int32, split embedding column on ',' and parse each float32
- Return Record{SourceFile, StartToken, Text, Embedding} — same type as fembed.Record
- Dims() returns len of first parsed embedding (detected at runtime, not from header)

New API endpoint: POST /api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy
  Body: {"path": "/absolute/path/to/file.embed"}
  Handler: same logic as importEmbedFile but uses TSVReader instead of fembed.Reader

Wire into router.go under /api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy.

Benefit: users with existing .embed files can ingest without running Python at all. The TSV float parsing is the only overhead vs .fembed.
close_reason: Implemented TSVReader + Streamer interface + /ingest/embed-file-legacy and /ingest/directory-legacy endpoints. No Python required. Shipped in f1f822a.

title: Add .embed TSV → .fembed converter to embed.py
description:
Add a --convert subcommand to python/embed.py that reads one or more existing .embed TSV files (columns: file_name, start_token, embedding, text) and writes them as .fembed binary files without re-running the model.

Usage: python embed.py --convert --embed-file foo.embed [--out-file foo.fembed]
       python embed.py --convert --embed-dir ./embeddings/  (batch convert *.embed in dir)

Implementation:
- Parse the TSV with csv.reader (tab delimiter), skip header row
- For each row: source_file=col[0], start_token=int(col[1]), embedding=[float(x) for x in col[2].split(',')], text=col[3]
- Detect dims from first row's embedding length
- Call write_fembed() with the collected records (already implemented)
- Default output: same path with .fembed extension replacing .embed

Edge cases: handle csv.field_size_limit (already set), skip empty rows, validate header, warn on dim mismatch across rows.

This enables zero-recompute migration of existing .embed files to the binary format for ingestion via POST /api/v1/ingest/embed-file.
close_reason: Implemented --convert mode in embed.py. Lazy model loading, single-file and batch-dir modes. Verified round-trip with Go embedfile reader. Shipped in 5dd0fe6.

title: Decide query-time vector search strategy
description: With pre-compute-only embedding (no live embedder), the HybridIndex cannot embed search queries for vector search. Two options to resolve: Option A (recommended) — fall back to BM25-only when no embedder is configured; HybridIndex.Search detects nil/stub embedder and skips vector ranking, returns BM25 results only. Option B — spawn a Python subprocess to embed a single query string and return binary float32 to stdout; acceptable if query latency ~500ms is tolerable. Decision affects: internal/search/hybrid.go (nil embedder guard), cmd/shuttle/main.go (embedder config), and whether Option B requires a minimal embed_query.py script. Resolve this before implementing the HNSW vector index.
close_reason: Resolved: implemented BM25-only fallback (Option A). HybridIndex.Embedder=nil skips vector search at query time. Shipped in 918ba96.

title: Spec out binary .fembed file format
description: Before implementing the Python and Go changes, pin down the exact byte layout for the new binary embedding file format (.fembed). Draft includes: 16-byte header (magic FEMB, version uint16, dims uint16, record_count uint32, 4 reserved bytes) and per-record layout (source_file_len uint32, source_file UTF-8, start_token int32, text_len uint32, text UTF-8, embedding float32 LE array). Review against: Python struct.pack compatibility, Go binary.Read compatibility, forward extensibility (version field), and whether start_token should be preserved or replaced with byte offsets. Output: a finalized spec (comment block or doc) that both python/embed.py and internal/ingest/embedfile/reader.go will implement against.
close_reason: Resolved: .fembed format finalized and implemented in python/embed.py and internal/ingest/embedfile/reader.go. Shipped in 918ba96.

title: Implement real text embedder (Qwen3/OpenAI)
description: Replace StubEmbedder in internal/ingest/embed.go with a real embedding model. StubEmbedder generates deterministic pseudo-random 64-dim vectors — semantically meaningless. A real implementation must: call an embedding API (Qwen3-embedding per AGENTS.md architecture, or OpenAI text-embedding-3-small as fallback); return properly L2-normalized float32 vectors; support both Embed(string) and EmbedBatch([]string) for efficiency; handle API errors and rate limits. Embedder is wired into both the Chunker (for storing chunk vectors) and HybridIndex (for query-time vector search). Vector dimensionality must be consistent between indexing and query time.
close_reason: Superseded by offline Qwen3 pipeline. Embeddings are pre-computed by python/embed.py and imported via the ingest API. HybridIndex uses nil embedder (BM25-only at query time) per the accepted architecture. No live embedder needed.

title: Plan local ASR transcriber (M1 Air, 8GB)
description:
Research and plan which local ASR model to use for the transcriber (replacing StubTranscriber), given M1 Air with 8GB RAM. Must run entirely locally — no API calls.

The transcriber receives an audio file path and must return speaker-diarized TranscriptSegment slices (SpeakerID, StartMs, EndMs, Text). The Transcriber interface is already defined in internal/ingest/transcribe.go.

## Hardware constraint
- Apple Silicon M1 Air, 8GB unified memory
- MLX already installed and working
- Python available

## Models to evaluate

### Transcription
- **mlx-whisper (large-v3)** — Apple MLX port of Whisper, runs natively on M1 Neural Engine. Best quality, ~3GB. Recommended starting point given MLX is already in use.
- **mlx-whisper (medium / small)** — faster, less accurate, ~1.5GB / ~500MB
- **faster-whisper (large-v3, int8)** — CTranslate2 backend, CPU+CoreML, ~2GB, no MLX dependency
- **whisper.cpp** — pure C++, CoreML acceleration, ~1-3GB depending on model size

### Speaker diarization (separate from transcription)
- **pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1** — requires HuggingFace token, ~500MB, runs on CPU/MPS
- **nemo-msdd** — NVIDIA NeMo, heavier dependency
- **simple-diarizer** — lightweight, less accurate but no auth needed
- Note: diarization is optional for MVP; can ship without it and add later

## Deliverable
Decision record specifying:
1. Chosen transcription model + backend (MLX vs faster-whisper vs whisper.cpp)
2. Whether to include diarization in v1 or defer it
3. How Go calls the transcriber: subprocess (like embed.py pattern) or REST
4. Go interface plan: how upload_handler.go calls the local transcriber

No implementation yet — planning only.
close_reason: Obsolete: the audio ingest path was deliberately removed in flying-shuttle-6fv.1.1 (transcribe.go, Transcriber interface, StubTranscriber, chunker.go all deleted; uploads are .txt/.md only). No local ASR transcriber is needed unless audio ingest is revived as a new feature.

title: Atlas Summariser interface + extractive fallback
description:
Phase B, the LLM-free half.

atlas.Summariser interface:
    Summarise(ctx, inputs []string) (Digest, error)
where Digest = {Title (<=6 words), Abstract (<=3 sentences), Keywords []string}.

Implement ExtractiveSummariser{BM25}: Title = top TF-IDF terms for the region,

title: Atlas Builder + POST /atlas/rebuild background job
description:
Ties Phases A/B/C together and exposes the rebuild trigger.

atlas.Builder{Store, Chunks, Embedder, Summariser}.Build(ctx) (*Build, error):
  A. partition chunks into regions (method from the clustering spike)
  B. digest each region (Summariser — extractive or LLM)
  C. links + per-chunk keywords + digest embeddings + RegionIndex load
Depends only on interfaces -> unit-testable with a stub Summariser and
hand-built vectors.

POST /atlas/rebuild -> background job:
  * ONE at a time — return 409 while a build is in progress.
  * low priority; check ctx.Err() between regions so shutdown mid-build stops
    promptly; a partial build is discarded, never persisted as ready.
  * started from main.go, tracked in the sync.WaitGroup, cancelled on
    SIGINT/SIGTERM — same pattern as indexer.Snapshotter / Backfiller.
  * shares a semaphore with the embed backfiller so a digest pass and a large
    embed batch never run concurrently.
Status polled by the UI like the ingest drawer
(data-on-interval__duration.2s until ready/failed).

Also: staleness hint — compare atlas_build.chunk_count to the current chunk
count; past ~10% drift the UI shows "Atlas is N chunks behind — rebuild".
No automatic rebuild.

Empty / not-yet-embedded corpus: Build errors cleanly with too few embedded
chunks; the pane explains "upload transcripts and let embeddings finish".

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Python subprocess resource caps + clean teardown
description:
Applies to BOTH Python sidecars: the embed server and the shared instruct-LLM
server. Section 9 of the plan.

  * Spawn with exec.CommandContext + own process group. On app exit the
    supervisor sends SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL after a short grace
    period. No orphaned python / MLX processes after the Go binary exits.
  * Single-flight: the Go side serialises requests to each server with a
    mutex; each server handles one batch at a time. Embed batch size capped
    (e.g. 16); instruct generation 1 at a time.
  * Memory caps inside each server: MLX memory limit + cache limit
    (mx.set_memory_limit, mx.set_cache_limit); release on idle.
  * Thread caps from the supervisor at spawn: OMP_NUM_THREADS,
    MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS set small.
  * Instruct LLM is lazy + idle-shed: starts on first use, exits itself after
    ~2 min idle to free ~2.5GB, supervisor restarts on next request. The
    ~300MB embedder may stay resident.
  * Global budget: a shared semaphore so an instruct-LLM digest pass and a
    large embed backfill never run at the same time.

Builds on the existing ingest.PythonEmbedder supervision. Coordinate with
flying-shuttle-hkc (which specifies the instruct server's contract).

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Source Atlas — transcript network for evidence discovery
description:
Build the Source Atlas: a derived, disposable, LLM-summarised NETWORK over the
transcript corpus that helps the author find source material to pull into the
outline. It is NOT part of the authored document and produces no prose.

CRITICAL — two separate graph-shaped things now exist and must never share
vocabulary, types, tables, packages or handler files:
  * The Outline  — the authored non-linear document. Elements: node, edge,
    thread, branch, snapshot, evidence. Packages internal/outline, dag, stitch.
  * The Source Atlas — this epic. Elements: region (a chunk cluster), link
    (weighted region<->region similarity), member chunk, centroid, digest.
    Package internal/atlas (new). Tables atlas_*. Undirected weighted graph,
    NO root, NO hierarchy, NO tiers, NO containment.
Forbidden: "atlas node" (it is a region), "atlas edge" (it is a link),
"outline region/cluster", storing a model.Node for a region, an edges row
referencing atlas_region, putting regions through outline.BuildTree.

The ONLY connection between the two: while exploring a region the author hits
"Add as evidence" on a member chunk, which flows through the EXISTING
POST /outline/nodes/{focusId}/evidence path. The Atlas never creates outline
nodes or edges.

Pipeline (memory-phased for M1 Air / 8GB): Phase A partition chunks into
regions (pure Go, no model) -> Phase B digest each region with the shared
instruct LLM (line-format, not JSON) -> Phase C build region link graph +
per-chunk keywords + embed digests into a small RegionIndex. One build at a
time; rebuild replaces the previous build wholesale; no state.json / snapshot
/ branch involvement.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Atlas region similarity-link graph
description:
Phase C, the graph-building half. internal/atlas/link.go.

For each region, compute cosine similarity of its centroid to every other
region's centroid; keep an undirected weighted link to its top-k nearest
regions above a similarity threshold (k and threshold in params_json).
Write atlas_region_link rows (canonical a<b ordering, one row per pair).

Region counts are in the hundreds, so an O(n^2) centroid scan is fine; no
HNSW needed for this.

Acceptance: unit test — a hand-built set of centroids produces the expected
links and weights; no duplicate pairs; no self-links.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Atlas schema + store (atlas_build / atlas_region / atlas_region_link / atlas_region_chunk)
description:
Migration + persistence layer for the Atlas. All tables atlas_-prefixed.
Nothing goes in internal/model (that package is the Outline's).

atlas_build:        id, created_at, status (building|ready|failed),
                    chunk_count, params_json, error
atlas_region:       id, build_id (FK, cascade), centroid_vec BLOB (float32 LE,
                    same encoding as chunks.embedding_vec), chunk_count,
                    digest_title, digest_abstract, digest_keywords
                    (newline-joined), digest_source ("llm:<model>" |
                    "extractive"), digest_vec BLOB (nullable until Phase C).
                    NO parent_region_id, NO tier — the Atlas is flat.
atlas_region_link:  build_id (FK), region_a_id (FK), region_b_id (FK),
                    weight REAL (centroid cosine). PK (region_a_id,
                    region_b_id) with CHECK (region_a_id < region_b_id) so a
                    pair is stored once, undirected.
atlas_region_chunk: region_id (FK), chunk_id (FK), distance REAL (cosine
                    distance to centroid, for ordering), keywords TEXT
                    (newline-joined extractive terms). PK (region_id,
                    chunk_id). Each chunk appears in exactly one region.

Store type: atlas.Region, atlas.Link, atlas.Digest, atlas.Build in
internal/atlas. Persistence in internal/atlas/store.go OR methods on
internal/store (decide). "One build at a time": creating a new build then
deleting the previous one cascade-wipes its regions/links/memberships.
No state.json / recovery / snapshot / branch involvement.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Spike: choose the chunk -> region clustering method
description:
Phase A of the Atlas build. UNRESOLVED — decide before any implementation.

Partition the full set of embedded chunks into many small "regions" (each
chunk belongs to exactly one region). Evaluate candidate methods against:
  * Pure Go, deterministic, runs in seconds on a few thousand chunk vectors.
  * Produces many small regions, rough target ~5-15 chunks each (soft, not a
    hard constraint).
  * No fixed cluster count baked in as a hard requirement.
  * Output must feed cleanly into building a kNN similarity graph over the
    region centroids (the "link" task).

Candidates on the table (do NOT default to k-means-with-magic-numbers):
  * community detection (Louvain / Leiden) on a chunk kNN graph
  * HDBSCAN-style density clustering
  * agglomerative clustering with a cosine-distance cut

Reuse only the low-level vector helpers from internal/search/cluster.go
(ingest.CosineSimilarity, centroid math) — NOT the EmbeddingClusterer /
LLMClusterer types (those are per-bullet-scoped, wrong granularity).

Deliverable: a decision record naming the method, its parameters, expected
runtime, and a rough Go implementation sketch. No production code.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Atlas per-chunk + per-region extractive keywords
description:
Extractive (TF-IDF, from the existing BM25 index stats) keyword tags:
  * per region -> atlas_region.digest_keywords (also the low-zoom graph label)
  * per member chunk -> atlas_region_chunk.keywords (the chunk-node label in
    the network view)

No LLM. internal/atlas/keywords.go. Computed during Phase C of the build.
Small, focused; split from the Summariser task if that one grows.

Acceptance: unit test on a synthetic corpus; keywords are the expected top
terms; deterministic.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Evidence-from-selection: offsets misaligned; enable attach from candidate card
description:
Two problems with attaching a transcript span as evidence:

1. Misalignment. app.js fillExcerptForm trims the selected text but does NOT adjust char_start/char_end, and reader segments render 'seg.Text + " "' so a selection reaching the end includes a synthetic trailing space — char_end can exceed the chunk length and AttachEvidence silently falls back to the whole chunk. Net: the stored excerpt text and its char offsets disagree, so the reader highlights the wrong range.

2. You can only attach evidence from inside the full transcript reader. Selecting text in an evidence-pane candidate card should offer 'Add as evidence' directly.

Fix: make AttachEvidence re-derive offsets by locating the selected text within chunk.Content (exact, then whitespace-normalized) and canonicalize the stored text to that exact substring. Add a floating 'Add as evidence' action for selections in .candidate-text, posting chunk_id + text to the existing endpoint.
close_reason: Shipped: outline.locateSelection + AttachEvidence realigns/canonicalizes text↔offsets; app.js fillExcerptForm trim-aware offsets; #candidate-attach floating button + form for selections in .candidate-text/.candidate-full → same /evidence endpoint (text-only, server locates); .float-tools shared. Tests: TestLocateSelection, TestAttachEvidence_realignsFromText, TestAttachEvidence_fromCandidateSelection.

title: Quote bullets: drop lock, add delete X, in-outline trim/splice selection
description:
The lock on evidence (chunk_ref) sub-bullets does nothing useful — Delete and SetTitle never check it and evidence bullets have no editable input. Replace it with direct manipulation:

1. Remove the lock icon from evidence bullets; stop setting Node.Locked in AttachEvidence.
2. Add an X button on each evidence bullet that deletes the quote (DELETE /outline/nodes/{id} already cascades the evidence row).
3. Let the user select a sub-range of a quote's text in the outline (main panel). While a selection is active in a .bullet-evidence, show two actions:
   a. Trim quote to selection — keep only the selected text.
   b. Remove selection from quote — splice the selected text out.
   Both update the evidence row (text + char offsets) and the node Body/Title. Text stays the verbatim source of truth for stitch/export.

New: store.UpdateEvidence; outline.Service.EditQuote(nodeID, op, start, end); POST /outline/quote-edit; #quote-tools toolbar + selection JS in app.js.
close_reason: Shipped: lock removed from evidence bullets (icon + Node.Locked on attach); X delete button; text-selection toolbar (#quote-tools) → POST /outline/quote-edit → outline.Service.EditQuote (trim/splice, offset tracking, ErrNoop guards); store.UpdateEvidence added. title: Atlas LLM digests via the shared instruct model
description:
Swap the extractive digester for the real one once the shared instruct model
is chosen. Depends on flying-shuttle-hkc (model decision) + the Summariser
interface + Builder.

LLMSummariser{Completer}: one LLM call per region, feeding up to ~15 member
chunks nearest the centroid (truncated). Output is LINE-FORMAT
(TITLE: / ABSTRACT: / KEYWORDS:), NOT JSON — small models are unreliable at
JSON (the flying-shuttle-hs8 finding). Parse leniently.

For a full rebuild that is ~25 calls; must finish in 1-2 min. Runs under the
resource discipline of the "Python subprocess resource caps" task: the
instruct server is single-flight, lazy, idle-shed, and holds the shared
semaphore so it never overlaps a big embed batch.

digest_source is recorded as "llm:<model>" vs "extractive" so the UI/tests
can tell which path produced a digest.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Atlas search box + focused-bullet affinity
description:
Two entry points into the region network. Depends on RegionIndex + Builder +
the embedder swap.

5b — Search the Atlas: a query box (atlasQuery signal) -> embed the query
(cheap with the 300MB embedder) -> RegionIndex.RankRegions -> show top
regions as entry points.

5c — Focused-bullet affinity: when a bullet is focused (focusId set), embed
that bullet's Title/Body text and rank regions against it — "Sources for this
bullet". Answers "where in my transcripts is there material for the point I'm
making?", which chunk-level keyword/passage search does poorly because a
bullet is prose. Read-only against the Outline (reads node.Title/Body, writes
nothing).

If the embedder is down, hide 5c and fall back to full browse — same
graceful-degradation contract as HybridIndex.Search.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Atlas network view — region graph, semantic zoom to chunks, detail pane
description:
Section 6 of the plan. A visual pan/zoom graph canvas of the region network
with semantic level-of-detail. Toggled by the atlasView signal (list|graph).
Depends on: schema, keywords, builder; also the embedder swap (for search).

REGION LEVEL (zoomed out, default):
  * one graph node per region; label = its top 2-3 keywords
    (digest_keywords), ALWAYS rendered and legible at low zoom — this is the
    map legend, do not declutter it away.
  * node size proportional to chunk_count; digest title on hover / in the
    detail pane.
  * graph edges = atlas_region_link rows; edge width proportional to weight.
  * force-directed layout computed CLIENT-SIDE with a fixed seed for
    stability across renders. (Server-persisted x/y coords are explicitly out
    of scope — later refinement.)

CHUNK LEVEL (zoomed into one region):
  * zooming past a threshold onto a region, or clicking "expand", replaces
    that region node with its member chunks as nodes; other regions dim /
    collapse.
  * each chunk node label = its per-chunk keywords
    (atlas_region_chunk.keywords).
  * optional edges between member chunks whose pairwise cosine exceeds a
    threshold.
  * zoom back out / "regions" control collapses the region.

RIGHT-HAND DETAIL PANE:
  * selecting a chunk node (atlasChunkId) -> full chunk text (chunk.Content or
    a transcript.Service window), source file, and the existing
    "Read in transcript ->" / "Add as evidence" actions.
  * selecting a region node (atlasRegionId) -> full digest + linked
    neighbours.

WIRING:
  * GET /atlas/graph.json -> region nodes + links;
    GET /atlas/graph.json?region={id} -> that region's chunk nodes +
    intra-region edges. Raw JSON to the client is deliberate — the renderer
    is imperative JS, like app.js.
  * renderer: a small graph library VENDORED under
    internal/web/static/vendor/ (no CDN — matches the Datastar vendoring).
    Candidates: Cytoscape.js, Sigma.js (WebGL), d3-force + canvas. Pick during
    implementation.
  * static/atlas_graph.js — the 2nd hand-written JS file in the project after
    app.js. Datastar signals stay the source of truth for selection so the
    list pane and the graph pane stay in sync.
  * read-only exploration; the only write is the evidence action on a
    selected chunk.

See source_atlas_plan.md (repo root) for the full plan.

title: Decide the shared local instruct LLM (stitcher + clusterer + Atlas digests, M1 Air 8GB)
description:
Research and decide the single local instruct LLM this project runs, on
M1 Air / 8GB RAM. Originally scoped for the stitcher glue-text generator
(replacing StubStitcher); it now also governs two further consumers that MUST
share the same model and the same OS process.

## The three consumers of the shared instruct model

1. **Stitcher glue text** — minimal connective prose between transcript
   excerpts at configurable verbosity (GlueLevel 0-100). Interactive
   (~1-5s per call acceptable).
2. **Per-bullet chunk clustering** — the dormant LLMClusterer
   (internal/search/cluster.go:185-278). See flying-shuttle-hs8. May instead
   be reworked to read the Source Atlas rather than call the LLM directly.
3. **Source Atlas region digests** — one {title, abstract, keywords} summary
   per chunk-cluster ("region") for the transcript network view. Batch:
   ~25 calls per rebuild, should finish in 1-2 min. See the Source Atlas epic
   and source_atlas_plan.md sections 2, 8, 9.

## Hard constraints

- Apple Silicon M1 Air, 8GB unified memory.
- EXACTLY ONE instruct model resident at a time. The ~300MB embedder
  (embeddinggemma-300m, see the "switch embedder" task) may be co-resident;
  a ~2.5GB instruct model on top of that plus the OS is the ceiling.
- 100% local, no API calls.
- MLX / mlx_lm ecosystem (same as the embedder).

## Models to evaluate

Rank by: fits in RAM at 4-bit; output quality for BOTH short generative glue
prose AND short structured summaries; inference speed.

- Qwen2.5-3B-4bit (MLX)         ~2GB   same ecosystem, strong instruction following
- Qwen2.5-7B-4bit (MLX)         ~4.5GB better quality, tight but fits
- Phi-3.5-mini-instruct 4bit    ~2.5GB strong on short-form generation
- Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 4bit    ~2GB   solid baseline
- Gemma-3-4B-it 4bit (MLX)      ~2.5GB good instruction following
- smollm2-1.7B (MLX)            ~1GB   very fast, may lack prose coherence

## Deliverable — a decision record (bd notes / AGENTS.md addition), NO code

1. Chosen model + quantization + exact MLX model ID.
2. Prompt formats:
   a. GlueLevel -> instruction mapping for the stitcher.
   b. Region-digest prompt. Line-format output (TITLE: / ABSTRACT: /
      KEYWORDS:), NOT JSON — small models are unreliable at JSON (this is the
      core flying-shuttle-hs8 finding).
   c. Per-bullet cluster prompt, only if hs8 keeps the direct-LLM path.
3. Process model: ONE supervised subprocess, reusing the
   ingest.PythonEmbedder supervision pattern (exec.CommandContext, own
   process group, restart with backoff, SIGTERM then SIGKILL on app exit).
   Sibling to embed_server.py. NOT Ollama, NOT a second always-on daemon.
   HTTP contract mirroring embed_server.py: GET /health, POST /complete
   {system, user} -> {text}.
4. Lifecycle / resource discipline (see source_atlas_plan.md section 9 and the
   "Python subprocess resource caps" task):
   - lazy start on first use; idle-shed after ~2 min to free the ~2.5GB;
     supervisor restarts on next request.
   - single-flight (one generation at a time).
   - thread caps (OMP_NUM_THREADS etc.) set by the Go supervisor at spawn.
   - MLX memory / cache limits set inside the server.
   - a shared semaphore with the embed backfiller so a digest pass and a
     large embed batch never run at the same time.
5. Go interface: a single shared Completer
   (Complete(ctx, systemPrompt, userPrompt) (string, error)) — already the
   interface at cluster.go:193 and in the stitch package — consumed by the
   stitcher, the clusterer, and the atlas digester alike.

Planning only. Implementation is separate, one task per consumer.

title: Plan local LLM for semantic chunk clustering (M1 Air, 8GB)
description:
Research and plan how to wire the existing LLMClusterer (internal/search/cluster.go:185-278) with a local LLM on M1 Air with 8GB RAM. The LLMClusterer identifies 3-4 sub-themes from a set of retrieved chunks using an LLM prompt; it is an alternative to EmbeddingClusterer (currently active).

Dependency: shares local LLM selection with flying-shuttle-hkc (stitcher). Only one local LLM should be resident in memory at a time on 8GB M1 Air.

Models to evaluate: same candidates as hkc. Key additional consideration: the clustering prompt asks for structured JSON output (array of {label, chunk_indices, confidence}), so the model must reliably follow JSON output instructions.

Deliverable — decision record (can be addendum to hkc decision) specifying:
1. Confirmed same model as stitcher, or different model with rationale
2. How the Completer interface (cluster.go:193) maps to the local model call
3. Whether to use a shared model process (one server for both stitcher + clusterer) or separate subprocesses
4. Config approach: env var to select EmbeddingClusterer vs LLMClusterer at startup

No implementation yet — planning only.
